target expression level and intracell ADC exposure are linearly related in cancer cells.

the relationship between target level and efficacy of ADC is complex and is likely to depend on the pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic characteristics of the ADC and the target.
there is a strong quantitative relationship (R2 ∼ 0.9-0.95) between target expression level (or number of target receptors) and intracellular exposure to ADC.
the target expression level is a critical parameter in determining the efficacy of an ADC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the efficacy of ADC is not only dependent on antigen expression level but also on the pharmacodynamic properties and the target antigen itself.
target expression level is a key determinant of intracellular ADC exposure, but not a key determinant of ADC efficacy.
the efficacy of ADCs is dependent on both target expression level and pharmacodynamic properties of the cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the target expression level can be used as an indicator for the ADC exposure inside cancer cells.
the target expression level is an important determinant of ADC exposure inside cancer cells, and therefore, should be considered in the design of clinical studies for ADCs.
target expression levels can be used to predict ADC efficacy, and therefore, the target expression level should not be ignored in ADC drug development.
